statement.name: Riemann's mapping theorem for Jordan regions
statement.definition: Every Jordan region Int(J), the interior of a Jordan curve J : [0,1] -> C, is conformally equivalent to the open unit disk B(0;1).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.4: over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to (2) for any Jordan curve J, Int(J) is a non-empty bounded connected open set, and to (3) every Jordan region is conformally equivalent to B(0;1).

statement.notation: RMT for simply connected open sets
statement.name: Riemann's mapping theorem
statement.definition: Every simply connected open subset U of C with U not equal to C is conformally equivalent to B(0;1).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.6 (Theorem 4.13 of Yokoyama's earlier paper [16]): over WKL0, ACA0 is equivalent to Riemann's mapping theorem for simply connected open sets. The paper gives a new nonstandard proof of ACA0 -> RMT.

statement.name: Weak Riemann's mapping theorem (semi-polygons)
statement.definition: For a simple semi-polygon gamma with interior D and c0 in D, D is conformally equivalent to B(0;1) via a biholomorphic uniformly continuous f with f(c0) = 0.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0.

statement.name: Cauchy's integral theorem for triangles
statement.definition: If f is holomorphic on an open subset D of C, then for every triangle abc inside D, the integral of f over the boundary of the triangle exists and equals 0.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3: equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (2 -> 1 is cited from [15]).

statement.notation: Effective integrability of continuous functions on open sets of C
statement.name: Effective line integrability of continuous complex functions
statement.definition: Every continuous function on an open D in C is effectively integrable: along every line or circular arc there is a modulus of integrability of the Riemann sums.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.1: equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass principle (weak form, Cauchy subsequence)
statement.definition: Every sequence of rationals in [0,1] has a (not necessarily fast) Cauchy subsequence: ∀(y_i) ∃f strictly monotone ∀n ∃s ∀v,w ≥ s |y_f(v) − y_f(w)| < 2^{-n}.
statement.facts: Corollary 6.6: RCA0 ⊢ StCOH ↔ BW_weak (instance-wise equivalent, Theorem 6.5). Theorem 6.7: Π11-conservative over RCA0 + Π01-CP and over RCA0 + Σ02-IA; RCA0 + BW_weak is Π02-conservative over PRA. Theorem 6.9: every bounded recursive sequence of reals has a low2 Cauchy subsequence, some has no computable one, some has no convergent subsequence computable in 0'. Close to the catalogue's sbwt but with sequences of rationals in [0,1].

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass principle (fast converging subsequence)
statement.definition: Every sequence of rationals in [0,1] has a subsequence converging with rate 2^{-n}.
statement.facts: Theorem 6.4: over RCA0 instance-wise equivalent to Σ01-WKL, hence equivalent to ACA0 (cited [86, Theorem I.9.1]).

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for Σ01 trees
statement.definition: Every infinite Σ01 0/1-tree has an infinite path.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ Σ01-WKL ↔ Π01-CA; instance-wise equivalent to Σ02-separation and to BW (Theorem 6.4).

statement.name: Π02 comprehension
statement.definition: For every Π02 formula ∀x∃y h(x,y,n)=0 the set {n | ∀x∃y h(x,y,n)=0} exists.
statement.facts: Theorems 7.8 and 7.12: over RCA0^ω, each instance of weak compactness in ℓ2 (weak-BW) is uniformly equivalent to an instance of Π02-CA; Corollary 7.13: degrees computing a weak cluster point of each computable bounded sequence in ℓ2 are exactly those ≥ 0''.

statement.name: Generalized Banach contraction conjecture
statement.definition: Every (m,γ)-g-contraction T on a presentable complete separable metric space has a fixed point; GBCC_m for fixed m, GBCC^cont for continuous T.
statement.facts: Theorem 9.2: WE-PA^ω1 + QF-AC^{0,0} ⊢ RT22 → GBCC_m for each m; RT2_{<∞} → GBCC^cont; RT2_{<∞} ∧ Σ03-IA → GBCC (over a third-order system, not RCA0).

statement.notation: closed => located (in compact complete separable metric spaces, or in [0,1])
statement.name: Every closed set is located
statement.definition: Located: the distance function d(x,C) exists as a continuous real-valued function. In a compact complete separable metric space (equivalently [0,1]) every closed set is located.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.8). Same for: closed => separably closed, separably closed => closed (Theorem 4.2, citing Brown), separably closed => located / weakly located (Theorem 5.10), closed + weakly located => located (Remark 5.3), closed + weakly located => separably closed (Theorem 5.11).

statement.notation: closed and separably closed => located / weakly located
statement.name: Closed and separably closed sets are located
statement.definition: In a compact complete separable metric space (or [0,1], or 2^N) every set which is both closed and separably closed is located (resp. weakly located). Weakly located: the predicate "exists eps>0 B(a, r+eps) intersect C empty" is Sigma^0_1.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.6, Theorem 5.8, together with "every closed set is weakly located"). Also, WKL0 proves every closed set in a compact space is weakly located (Lemma 5.4); separably closed + weakly located => located and closed in RCA0 (Theorem 5.5); for separably closed sets located iff weakly located in RCA0 (Theorem 5.7); closed + located => separably closed in RCA0 (Theorem 4.5).

statement.notation: strong Tietze theorem for separably closed sets (with modulus of uniform continuity)
statement.name: Strong Tietze theorem for separably closed sets
statement.definition: For X compact complete separable metric (or [0,1]), C a separably closed subset and f: C -> R uniformly continuous with modulus of uniform continuity, there is F in C(X) extending f.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.14).

statement.notation: Tietze extension theorem for separably closed sets and continuous f (no modulus)
statement.name: Tietze extension for separably closed sets, continuous functions
statement.definition: For X compact complete separable metric (or [0,1]), C separably closed and f: C -> R continuous, there is a continuous F with F restricted to C equal to f.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.9).

statement.notation: Strong Tietze for weakly located closed sets (Theorem 6.4)
statement.name: Strong Tietze theorem for weakly located closed sets
statement.definition: X compact complete separable metric space, C a weakly located closed subset, f: C -> R uniformly continuous with modulus and uniform code: then f extends to F in C(X).
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Theorem 6.4); fails in REC without weak locatedness (Lemma 6.16).

statement.name: WKL0 plus 'if exactly one Z satisfies φ(X,Z) then it is computable in X'
statement.definition: ∀X (if (∃ exactly one Z) φ(X,Z) then (∃Z)(Z ≤_T X and φ(X,Z))) for L2-formulas φ with no other free set variables.
statement.facts: WKL0 plus this scheme has first order part Σ⁰₁-PA, the same as WKL0 (Corollary 7.9, from Theorem 7.8).

statement.name: Π⁰₁ formula with finitely different solutions
statement.definition: A Π⁰₁ formula ψ̃(X) built from Kučera's pair (Lemma 10.1) and a Π⁰₁ sentence provable in Σ⁰₂-PA but not Σ⁰₁-PA.
statement.facts: WKL0 proves ∃Xψ̃(X); RCA0 proves any two solutions differ finitely; WKL0 does not prove (∃ recursive X)ψ̃(X); RCA0 does not prove ∃Xψ̃(X). Refutes Tanaka's conjecture that WKL0 is conservative over RCA0 for sentences '∃ countably many X φ(X)' (Remark 10.9).

statement.name: Cohesion for weakly represented families
statement.definition: For every weakly represented family F of sets there exists an F-cohesive set. (Weakly represented families: Definitions 4-6.)
statement.facts: COHW implies COH trivially (Remark 8). Theorem 29: over RCA0, COH does not imply COHW, even for ω-models. Theorem 37: COHW implies AVOID for ω-models; not in all non-ω-models. Theorem 43: COHW implies HI. Corollary 45: over RCA0 + BΣ2, DOM implies COHW. Proposition 46: over RCA0 + DOM, COH implies COHW; also over RCA0 + WKL0, COH ↔ COHW.

statement.name: Maximal almost disjoint family principle
statement.definition: There exists a weakly represented infinite family of infinite sets, pairwise almost disjoint, such that every infinite set in S meets some member in an infinite set.
statement.facts: Theorem 55: an ω-model satisfies MAD iff it does not satisfy DOM.

statement.name: Maximal independent family principle
statement.definition: There exists a weakly represented family of infinite sets that is maximal independent.
statement.facts: Theorem 56: an ω-model satisfies MIND iff it does not satisfy BI.

statement.name: Decomposition (weak decomposition) of an e-matroid into 1-dimensional subspaces
statement.definition: Given an e-matroid (M,D), produce f: M→N with f(n)=0 iff n is zero element, and f(n)=f(m) iff {n,m} dependent (weak version: only the last condition).
statement.facts: Theorem 2.2.2: WDM ≡sW DM ≡sW LPO^ (parallelization of LPO). Theorem 2.3.1: reverse-mathematics versions DM and WDM are equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Characteristic function of the finite dependent sets of an e-matroid
statement.definition: Input an e-matroid (M,D), output the characteristic function of range(D).
statement.facts: Theorem 2.2.1: DEP_W ≡sW LPO^.

statement.name: Enumerated matroid
statement.definition: Pair (M,D), M ⊆ N, D: N→[N]^<N enumerating the finite dependent sets of a matroid.
statement.facts: Computably obtained from countable vector spaces and graphs with enumerated edges (Lemmas 2.1.4, 3.2.1).

statement.name: Existence of a 1-dimensional subspace of a countable vector space of dimension > 1
statement.definition: Given a countable vector space of dimension greater than 1, return a 1-dimensional subspace.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.1.1: PS_W ≤sW L_W and L implies PS over RCA0. Theorem 3.2.2: L_W ≤sW LPO^. Theorem 3.3.1: L ↔ ACA0 over RCA0 (using DHKLMM for the lower bound).

statement.name: Nontrivial proper subspace of a countable vector space (Weihrauch problem)
statement.definition: Given a countable vector space of dimension > 1, return a nontrivial proper subspace.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.2.6: SEP ≤W PS_W; Theorem 3.2.8: PS_W ≤W WKL_W ⋆ C_N; Corollary 3.2.9: WKL ≤W PS_W ≤W WKL ⋆ C_N. Exact degree open (Chapter 6). PS_W is the problem form of the catalogue sentence nps (PS).

statement.name: Finite-dimensional nontrivial proper subspace of a countable vector space (Weihrauch)
statement.definition: Pairs (V,S) with V a countable vector space of dimension > 1 and S a finite-dimensional nontrivial proper subspace.
statement.facts: PS^{<N}_W ≤sW L_W by definition; open whether LPO^ ≤W PS^{<N}_W (Chapter 6).

statement.name: Nonempty finite-dimensional saturated subgraph (finite union of connected components)
statement.definition: Given a graph G, return a nonempty union of finitely many connected components; the starred version restricts to graphs with at least one edge.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.1.2: PSG^{<N}_W ≡sW LPO^; Corollary 4.1.3: the starred version ≡sW LPO^.

statement.name: Nontrivial finite-dimensional subspace of a nontrivial e-matroid
statement.definition: Given a nontrivial e-matroid, return a nontrivial finite-dimensional subspace.
statement.facts: Corollary 4.1.4: PSM_W ≡sW LPO^.

statement.name: Nontrivial proper saturated subgraph
statement.definition: Given a countable graph with at least two connected components, return a nonempty union of connected components that is not the whole graph.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.2.1: C_N ≤sW PSG_W; Theorem 4.2.2: WKL_W ≤W PSG_W; Corollary 4.2.3: PSG_W ≰W WKL_W; Theorem 4.2.4: PSG_W ≤W WKL_W ⋆ C_N.

statement.name: Decomposition of a countable vector space into 1-dimensional subspaces
statement.definition: Every countable vector space has a decomposition into 1-dimensional subspaces (analogue of Definition 2.3.1).
statement.facts: Theorem 5.1.1: DV ↔ ACA0 over RCA0. DV ≤W LPO^ (Chapter 5, from Theorem 2.1.1); whether DV ≡W LPO^ is open.

statement.name: Probabilistic choice on ω×2^ω
statement.definition: Multi-valued function sending a tree T of positive measure (w.r.t. the measure on ω×2^ω with first value n of probability 2^{-n-1}, then fair bits) to its set of infinite paths [T].
statement.facts: PC_{ω×2^ω} ≡sW PC_{ω^ω} (Theorem 5.2); PC_{ω×2^ω} ≡sW WWKL_{≠0^ω} ≡sW WWKL_{1-Ran} (Theorem 5.1); WWKL <W PC_{ω×2^ω} <W WWKL′ (Brattka–Pauly [7]); LPO ≤W PC_{ω×2^ω} (Prop. 6.6); Cω × WWKL ≡sW PC_{ω×2^ω} (Brattka–Gherardi–Hölzl).

statement.name: Probabilistic choice on Baire space
statement.definition: Multi-valued function sending a tree in ω^{<ω} of positive measure (product measure with value n of probability 2^{-n-1}) to its set of infinite paths.
statement.facts: PC_{ω^ω} ≡sW PC_{ω×2^ω} (Theorem 5.2), PC′_{ω^ω} ≡sW PC′_{ω×2^ω} (Corollary 5.3); answers negatively whether WWKL′ ≤W PC_{ω^ω}.

statement.name: Jump of probabilistic choice on ω×2^ω
statement.definition: Input a sequence of trees converging pointwise to a tree of positive measure; output a path of the limit tree.
statement.facts: WWKL′ ⋆ WWKL′ ≡W PC′_{ω×2^ω} (Theorem 4.5/4.6); PC′_{ω×2^ω} ⋆ PC′_{ω×2^ω} ≡W PC′_{ω×2^ω} (Theorem 4.5); WWKL′ ≤sW PC′_{ω×2^ω} but PC′_{ω×2^ω} ≰W WWKL′ (Prop. 4.7); PC_{ω×2^ω} ⋆ WWKL′ ≡W PC′_{ω×2^ω} (Prop. 6.5).

statement.name: Jump of WWKL returning a 2-random path
statement.definition: Sends (T_i) in limtree^{>0}_{2^ω} to a path of T_∞ which is 2-random relative to (T_i).
statement.facts: WWKL′_{2-Ran} ≡W WWKL′ ⋆ WWKL′ (Theorem 4.6); ≡sW PC′_{ω×2^ω} (Theorem 4.3); WWKL′_{2-Ran} ≤sW WWKL′′ and WWKL′′ ≰W WWKL′_{2-Ran} (Prop. 4.8).

statement.name: Identity on sequences with finitely many ones
statement.definition: Identity function restricted to the binary sequences with only finitely many ones.
statement.facts: Id_Fin ≤sW WWKL (Lemma 6.3, Brattka and Hölzl).

statement.notation: HT^{≤2}_2 with apartness (= FUT^{≤2}_2); also HT^{≤n}_k with t-apartness
statement.name: Bounded Hindman theorem with apartness condition
statement.definition: HT^{≤n}_k: every k-coloring of N has an infinite H with FS^{≤n}(H) monochromatic; with t-apartness H must satisfy μ_t(x)<λ_t(x′) for x<x′ in H (largest exponent below least exponent in base t).
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 (and mutually strongly computably reducible) to FUT^{≤n}_k, any t (Prop. 2, Cor. 3). HT^{≤n}_{2k} implies HT^{≤n}_k with apartness by sc reduction (Lemma 4). HT^{≤2}_2 with apartness implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Prop. 5); HT^{≤2}_4 implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Thm 6); IPT^2_2 ≤sc HT^{≤2}_4 (Cor. 11), also ≤sc FUT^{≤2}_2. Open whether ACA0 implies HT^{≤2}_2.

statement.notation: HT^{=n}_k with apartness (= FUT^{=n}_k), HT^{=3}_2 with apartness
statement.name: Hindman theorem for sums of exactly n terms with apartness
statement.definition: Every k-coloring of N has an infinite 2-apart H with FS^{=n}(H) monochromatic.
statement.facts: HT^{=3}_2 with apartness is equivalent to RT^3_2 (so to ACA0) over RCA0 (Thm 7); for n>=3, k>1 HT^{=n}_k with apartness is equivalent to HT^{=3}_2 with apartness (Prop. 8); HT^{=n}_k ≤sc RT^n_k; IPT^2_2 ≤sc HT^{=2}_2 with apartness (Thm 10); HT^{=n}_k ≤sc HT^{=m}_k when n divides m (Prop. 9); no lower bounds are known without apartness.

statement.name: Hindman-type principles with some pair of sum lengths
statement.definition: For every 2-coloring of N there are an infinite H and a<b (resp. some a>=3) such that FS^{{a,b}}(H) (resp. FS^{{a}}(H)) is monochromatic.
statement.facts: With apartness each is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Thms 12, 13); HT^{∃{a<b}}_2 with apartness ≤sc RT^3_8.

statement.name: Increasing polarized Hindman theorem for pairs
statement.definition: For every 2-coloring f of N there are infinite H_1,H_2 (union apart) and a color k with f(x_1+x_2)=k for all increasing (x_1,x_2) in H_1 x H_2.
statement.facts: IPT^2_2 and IPHT^2_2 with apartness are equivalent over RCA0, and IPT^2_2 ≤sc IPHT^2_2 with apartness (Thm 14); IPHT^2_2 with apartness ≤sc HT^{!ω}_2 with apartness (Prop. 16).

statement.name: Hindman theorem for exactly large sums
statement.definition: For every 2-coloring f of N there is an infinite H such that all sums of exactly large subsets of H (|S| = min S + 1) have the same color.
statement.facts: Follows from RT^{!ω}_2 by a strong computable reduction (obvious); HT^{!ω}_2 with 2-apartness implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Prop. 15).

statement.name: Bounded Finite Unions Theorem
statement.definition: Block-sequence version of Hindman theorem with unions of at most (exactly) n blocks.
statement.facts: Equivalent to HT^{≤n}_k (resp. HT^{=n}_k) with t-apartness over RCA0, mutually strongly computably reducible (Prop. 2).

statement.name: Clopen Lipschitz determinacy in the Cantor space
statement.definition: Every Lipschitz game G_L(A,B) on 2^N with Δ⁰₁ payoff sets A and B is determined (player I wins iff not(A(f) <-> B(g)); II wins iff A(f) <-> B(g)).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.11: over RCA0, Δ⁰₁-Det*_L is equivalent to WKL0 (Proposition 3.9(1): WKL0 proves it). Theorem 1.3(2): also equivalent over RCA0 to (Δ⁰₁,Σ⁰₁)-Det*_L and (Σ⁰₁,Δ⁰₁)-Det*_L (Proposition 3.12). Answers Problem 4.17 of Loureiro's thesis; strengthens Chan's result for (Σ⁰₁∧Π⁰₁,Δ⁰₁)-Det*_L.

statement.name: Clopen Wadge determinacy in the Cantor space
statement.definition: Determinacy of Wadge games on 2^N with Δ⁰₁ payoff set for player I (and Σ⁰ₙ for player II).
statement.facts: Proposition 3.9(2): RCA0 proves (Δ⁰₁,Σ⁰ₙ)-Det*_W for every n>0; also (Δ⁰₁,Σ⁰ₙ)-SLO*_W and (Σ⁰ₙ,Δ⁰₁)-SLO*_W (Corollary 5.3(1)).

statement.name: Open Lipschitz/Wadge determinacy in the Cantor space
statement.definition: Determinacy of Lipschitz (resp. Wadge) games on 2^N whose payoff sets are Σ⁰₁ (resp. Σ⁰₁ for I and Σ⁰₁∧Π⁰₁ for II).
statement.facts: Corollary 4.5: ACA0 proves Σ⁰₁-Det*_L and Σ⁰₁-Det*_W. Theorem 5.5: over RCA0, ACA0, Σ⁰₁-Det*_L, WKL0 + Σ⁰₁-Det*_W and WKL0 + Σ⁰₁-SLO*_{L/W} are pairwise equivalent. Theorem 5.7: over RCA0, ACA0, (Σ⁰₁,Σ⁰₁∧Π⁰₁)-Det*_{L/W} and (Σ⁰₁,Σ⁰₁∧Π⁰₁)-SLO*_{L/W} are pairwise equivalent. Open: whether Σ⁰₁-Det*_W implies ACA0 (Problem 3).

statement.name: Lipschitz/Wadge semi-linear ordering principle in the Cantor space
statement.definition: For all payoff sets A in Γ1 and B in Γ2, either A is Lipschitz (Wadge) reducible to B or the complement of B is reducible to A, formalized in second-order arithmetic.
statement.facts: Proposition 5.4: over WKL0, Σ⁰₁-SLO*_W implies ACA0; Proposition 5.6: over RCA0, (Σ⁰₁,Σ⁰₁∧Π⁰₁)-SLO*_W implies ACA0. Open Problems 2 to 6 (Section 6): is Δ⁰₁-SLO*_L equivalent to WKL0; is Σ⁰₁-SLO*_L or Σ⁰₁-SLO*_W equivalent to ACA0; does Σ⁰₁-SLO*_W imply WKL0.

statement.name: Closed non-open sets of the Cantor space have nonempty boundary
statement.definition: Every closed and not open set in the Cantor space has nonempty boundary (combinatorial version of a result of Shafer).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.7: over RCA0, ACA0, (DP) and 'each infinite binary tree has a leftmost path' are equivalent. RCA0 + (DP) extends WKL0 (proof of Theorem 4.4). The leftmost-path statement here is for infinite binary trees, not for trees on N<N.

statement.name: Ramsey property of Σ¹₁ sets
statement.definition: Every Σ¹₁ set of reals has the property of Ramsey (a homogeneous infinite set accepting or avoiding it).
statement.facts: ACA0 proves that Σ11-MI0 is equivalent to Σ11-RT (Tanaka [Tan89]).

statement.name: Ramsey property of Δ¹₁ sets
statement.definition: Every Δ¹₁ set of reals has the property of Ramsey.
statement.facts: ACA0 proves that Π11-TR is equivalent to Δ11-RT (Tanaka [Tan89]).

statement.name: Π¹₁ transfinite recursion
statement.definition: Transfinite recursion along well-orderings for Π¹₁ formulas.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Δ11-RT over ACA0 (Tanaka).

statement.name: Σ¹₁ monotone inductive definitions
statement.definition: ACA0 plus: every Σ¹₁-definable monotone operator has a smallest fixed point.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ11-RT over ACA0 (Tanaka); much weaker than Π12-CA0.

statement.name: System of autonomous iterated Ramseyness
statement.definition: ACA0 in the language with set terms R_x X phi(x,X) giving, for first-order phi, a set which after removing an initial segment is homogeneous for {X : phi(x,X)}.
statement.facts: Theorem 1.3.4 (main theorem): the R-calculus and Π12-CA0 prove the same Π11-sentences of L2.

statement.name: Möllerfeld theory aame (comprehension for game quantifiers)
statement.definition: Subsystem of second order arithmetic with comprehension for first-order formulas containing game quantifiers.
statement.facts: Proves the same Π11-sentences as Π12-CA0 (Möllerfeld [Möl02]).

statement.name: Calculi of iterated (non)monotone inductive definitions
statement.definition: µ-calculus: iterated monotone inductive definitions; σ-calculus: nonmonotone analogue; σ+-calculus: σ-calculus with additional transfinite induction.
statement.facts: µ-calculus, σ-calculus and aame prove the same L2-sentences and the same Π11-sentences as Π12-CA0 (Möllerfeld); the paper shows the σ+-calculus proves the same Π11-sentences as Π12-CA0.

statement.name: Monotone convergence theorem for nets indexed by N (type 2 functionals) and range of type-three functionals
statement.definition: MCT^N_net: every increasing net in [0,1] indexed by N ≡ N^N → N converges. RANGE^1: (∀G^3)(∃X^1)(∀n^0)(n ∈ X ↔ (∃Y^2)(G(Y) = n)).
statement.facts: Corollary 3.9: Z_2^Ω + QF-AC^{0,2} proves MCT^N_net → RANGE^1 (via Theorems 3.5 and 3.7 lifted one type up). RANGE^1 first introduced in [45, §3.7].

statement.notation: (a) Heine-Borel compact complete metric space over N^N is totally bounded
statement.name: Effective total boundedness of Heine-Borel compact complete metric spaces over Baire space
statement.definition: Complete metric space D over N^N (Def 3.10); Heine-Borel compact: every cover by balls B(e,Y(e)), Y: D -> R+, has a finite subcover (Def 3.11); totally bounded: a sequence of finite sequences of points approximating every point (Def 3.12). Items (b) countable Heine-Borel compactness, (c) sequential compactness instead.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.13: ACA_0^ω + IND proves that each of (a), (b), (c) implies BOOT. Corollary 3.14: ACA_0^ω + IND proves (a) → QF-AC^{0,1}. Corollaries 3.15, 3.16: Z_2^Ω proves the type-N analogue (d) implies RANGE^1 and QF-AC^{0,2}.

statement.name: Separably closed sets (given by nets) in R are RM-closed
statement.definition: A separably closed set in R is given by a net x_d: D -> Q with D subset of N^N; x in S iff (∀k)(∃d ∈ D)(|x - x_d| ≤ 1/2^k). CLO: such a set is RM-closed (complement of an RM-open set, Π^0_1 definable).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.19: ACA_0^ω + ∆-CA proves CLO → RANGE. Corollary 3.20: the same holds with "RM-closed" replaced by "located".

statement.name: Rado selection lemma for collections indexed by Baire space
statement.definition: For a collection of finite sets A_i indexed by N^N and choice functions F_J for A_j, j in J, for each finite J, there is a choice function F for the whole collection such that for all finite J there is a finite K ⊇ J with F(j) = F_K(j) for j in J.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.23: RCA_0^ω proves Rado(N^N) → BOOT (without countable choice or ∆-CA).

statement.name: Formally real fields over Baire space are orderable
statement.definition: Fields K over N^N (|K| subset of N^N with equivalence relation and operations); formally real: no sum of squares equals 0; ORD: every formally real field over N^N is orderable.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.28: ACA_0^ω + ∆-CA proves ORD → SEP^1. The field built is countable, so ORD restricted to countable fields already gives SEP^1.

statement.name: Every field over Baire space embeds in an algebraically closed field over Baire space
statement.definition: Every field over N^N is isomorphic to a sub-field of an algebraically closed field over N^N.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.31: ACA_0^ω + ∆-CA proves ALCL → BOOT.

statement.name: Unique algebraic closure for fields over Baire space
statement.definition: A field over N^N has a unique algebraic closure: for two algebraic closures H_i: K -> K_i there is an isomorphism H: K_1 -> K_2 with H∘H_1 = H_2 on K.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.33: ACA_0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} proves UACL → SEP^1.

statement.name: Extension of automorphisms of F(α) to the algebraic closure, for fields over Baire space
statement.definition: F a field over N^N with algebraic closure, α in the closure, φ an F-automorphism of F(α): φ extends to an F-automorphism of the algebraic closure.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.38: ACA_0^ω proves AUTO → SEP^1.

statement.notation: (a) commutative ring / (b) integral domain over N^N has a maximal ideal
statement.name: Existence of maximal ideals for rings over Baire space
statement.definition: Commutative ring (resp. integral domain) R with |R| subset of N^N; ideal M maximal if for all r not in M there is s with r×s - 1 in M.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.41: over ACA_0^ω, either (a) or (b) implies BOOT.

statement.name: Every infinite tree on {0,1} has a leftmost path
statement.definition: Every infinite tree T on {0,1} has a path which is least in the lexicographic order.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Lemma 3.1).

statement.notation: Riesz representation (Hilbert space, representability of bounded linear functionals)
statement.name: Every bounded linear functional on a Hilbert space is representable by an inner product
statement.definition: For every bounded linear functional f on a (separable) Hilbert space H there is y in H with f(x) = <x,y> for all x. Close to the catalogue's Weihrauch problem frr, but stated here as a sentence for arbitrary Hilbert spaces, so not matched.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to ACA0; the reversal uses l2. Equivalent over RCA0 to: every bounded linear functional on a Banach or Hilbert space has a norm; its kernel is located (Theorems 13.2-13.4).

statement.notation: Mean ergodic theorem for Hilbert spaces
statement.name: Von Neumann's mean ergodic theorem (nonexpansive operators or isometries on a Hilbert space)
statement.definition: For every Hilbert space H, nonexpansive linear operator (or isometry) T and point x, the averages S_n x = (x + Tx + ... + T^{n-1}x)/n converge.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0, for both nonexpansive operators and isometries (Theorems 14.1 and 15.3). Even assuming P_M x exists and equals 0, convergence needs ACA0 (Theorem 15.3). Over RCA0 the existence of P_N x, the decomposition x = x_M + x_N and the convergence of S_n x are equivalent (Theorem 14.2).

statement.notation: closed / separably closed / located closed sets in complete separable metric spaces
statement.name: Notions of closed subsets and their relations
statement.definition: Closed (complement of an open set), separably closed (closure of a countable sequence) and located (with a continuous distance function) subsets of complete separable metric spaces.
statement.facts: Closed and located is the same as separably closed and located over RCA0 (Theorem 5.1). Over RCA0, ACA0 is equivalent to: in a compact space every closed set is separably closed; in [0,1] every separably closed set is closed; every closed set in [0,1] is located; every open set has a closure; d(x,C) exists for closed C in compact spaces. Pi11-CA0 is equivalent to: in Baire space every closed set is separably closed; every closed set in Baire space is located; for Gδ sets S of [0,1] the distance d(0,S) exists; every analytic set has a closure (Theorems 5.3, 5.4, 6.1, 7.1, 7.2). Several of these are credited to Brown, Giusto-Simpson, Giusto-Marcone, Hirst.

statement.notation: closed subspace vs closed linear set, location and projections in Hilbert spaces
statement.name: Closed subspaces, closed linear sets, locating functions and projections
statement.definition: Three notions of closed subspace of a Hilbert or Banach space: closed linear set, closed subspace (separably closed linear set), located closed subspace.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, ACA0 is equivalent to: every closed subspace is a closed linear set; every closed subspace is located; for every closed subspace and point the projection or distance exists (Theorems 11.1, 12.5). The corresponding statements for closed linear sets are implied by Pi11-CA0 and imply ACA0 (Theorems 11.1, 12.6); their exact strength is left open (Section 16).

statement.notation: bases and independent generating sequences in Hilbert and Banach spaces
statement.name: Existence of orthonormal bases and independent generating sequences
statement.definition: Every Hilbert space has an orthonormal basis; every Banach space has an independent generating sequence (linearly independent elements with dense linear span).
statement.facts: Every Hilbert space has an orthonormal basis, and every infinite dimensional Banach space has an independent generating sequence, in RCA0. Every Banach space has an independent generating sequence in RCA0 plus the disjunction of WKL and Sigma2 induction (Theorem 10.10); whether this is provable in RCA0 alone is left open (Section 16).

statement.name: Compactness theorem for first-order logic
statement.definition: If T is a set of first-order sentences and every finite subset of T is satisfiable, then T is satisfiable.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Lemma 1.5, citing Simpson IV.3.3).

statement.name: Existence of 1-point homogeneous, 1-homogeneous, strongly 1-homogeneous models of complete consistent theories
statement.definition: Every complete consistent theory has a model that is 1-point homogeneous (resp. 1-homogeneous, strongly 1-homogeneous) in the sense of Definition 1.1.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorems 2.2 (Lange), 2.3, Prop. 3.2). Restricted to theories with only principal types the strongly 1-homogeneous version is still equivalent to WKL0 (Theorem 2.4, Prop. 5.6).

statement.name: Every complete consistent theory has a homogeneous model
statement.definition: Every complete consistent theory has a homogeneous model in the sense of Definition 1.1(6).
statement.facts: Provable from RCA0 + BΣ02; exact strength asked in Question 2.5 (open: is it equivalent to RCA0 + BΣ02?).

statement.name: Every complete consistent theory with countably many types has a saturated model
statement.definition: Every complete consistent theory with a coded sequence of all its types has a saturated model (Definition 1.1(7)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.10, Cor. 3.4, Prop. 6.5). The ∅-saturated version is provable in WKL0 (Prop. 3.3).

statement.notation: Saturated model existence with pairwise full amalgamation
statement.name: Every complete consistent theory with countably many types whose types have the pairwise full amalgamation property has a saturated model
statement.definition: A complete consistent theory with countably many types whose sequence of all types has the pairwise full amalgamation property (Definition 2.11) has a saturated model.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 + (WKL0 v IΣ02) (Prop. 2.13); equivalent to WKL0 v IΣ02 over RCA0 + BΣ02 (Theorem 2.14, Prop. 7.17); not implying WKL0 v IΣ02 over RCA0 alone (Cor. 2.19); provable from WKL0 v Π01GA (Cor. 2.18). Open: equivalent to WKL0 v Π01GA over RCA0 (Question 2.20)?

statement.notation: 1PT FREE, 1PT FULL, PW FREE, PW FULL, FIN FREE, FIN FULL
statement.name: Type amalgamation properties of the sequence of all types
statement.definition: Six properties of a sequence X of all types of a complete consistent theory (1-point, pairwise, finite; free or full amalgamation).
statement.facts: For each pair A, B the statement (forall X)[A(X) -> B(X)] is equivalent over RCA0 to WKL0 or to WKL0 v IΣ02 according to Figure 1 (Theorem 2.24); e.g. (FIN FREE -> 1PT FULL) implies WKL0 (Theorem 2.23(iii), Prop. 6.4); WKL0 proves 1PT FREE -> FIN FULL (Theorem 2.22(i)); RCA0 + IΣ02 proves 1PT FREE -> FIN FREE and 1PT FULL -> FIN FULL (Theorem 2.22(ii),(iii)).

statement.notation: Elementary embedding of a countable sequence of models; universal models
statement.name: Existence of a model into which every model of a sequence embeds elementarily; universal models
statement.definition: For a complete theory T and a sequence of models of T there is a model of T into which each embeds elementarily; consequently universal models exist when all models are listed, or when the number of n-types is bounded by a function f.
statement.facts: Provable in WKL0 (Theorems 2.25, 2.27, Cor. 2.26); reversals not claimed.

statement.notation: Embedding of partial orders into the preorder of models
statement.name: Every partial order embeds into the preorder of models of a theory with infinitely many n-types under elementary embedding
statement.definition: If T has infinitely many n-types for some n, every partial order embeds into the preorder of models of T under elementary embeddability.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to WKL0 + not-ACA0 (Theorem 2.28).

statement.notation: Existence of models with a sequence of indiscernibles
statement.name: Every complete consistent theory has a model with a sequence of indiscernibles
statement.definition: Every complete consistent countable theory has a model with a sequence of indiscernibles (Definition 2.29).
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.32); even the order-indiscernibles version implies WKL0 (Prop. 4.7).

statement.name: Los–Vaught theorem (a theory with exactly one countable model is complete)
statement.definition: If T has only one countable model then for every sentence φ, T ⊢ φ or T ⊢ ¬φ.
statement.facts: Part (ii): over RCA0, every deductively-closed theory with exactly one model up to isomorphism is complete. Part (iii): the statement of part (i) is equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (proof of the reversal: if WKL0 fails, a theory built from a consistent theory with no models and DLO has one model but does not decide the 0-ary sentence R).

statement.name: Every deductively-closed consistent theory is satisfiable
statement.definition: Every deductively-closed consistent theory is satisfiable; every consistent complete theory is satisfiable and every deductively-closed consistent theory extends to a complete consistent one.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Simpson, Thm II.8.4); contrasted with Theorem 1.4 (full completeness is equivalent to WKL0).

statement.name: Type omitting theorem for complete theories and nonprincipal types
statement.definition: If T is a complete theory and p(x̄) a nonprincipal type, then T has a model omitting p.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Harizanov, Thm 6.1; easy Henkin-style construction).

statement.name: Engeler–Ryll-Nardzewski–Svenonius conditions on a complete theory T
statement.loc: Theorem 2.1 and the definitions around Theorem 2.6
statement.definition: S1: T has exactly f(n) n-types for a function f; S2: at most f(n) n-types; S3: finitely many n-types for each n; S4: T is aleph0-categorical; S5: all types of T are principal. Variants S3': for each n there is k such that any k+1 n-ary formulas contain two T-equivalent ones; S5': every model realizes only principal types; S5'': an atomic model realizes all types.
statement.facts: Over RCA0: (S1→S2), (S2→S3), (S3→S5), (S1→S4), (S4→S5) are provable (Theorem 2.3); (S2→S1) (Prop 6.11), (S2→S4) (Cor 6.14), (S3→S2) (Prop 6.12), (S5→S3) (Prop 4.5), (S5→S4) (Prop 4.6) each imply ACA0; (S4→S3) is equivalent to WKL0 (Props 3.5 and 5.6); (S4→S1) and (S4→S2) each imply WKL0 and are provable in ACA0, exact strength open (Question 2.5). RCA0 proves S3↔S3', S5↔S5', S5↔S5'' (Theorem 2.6). Table of all equivalences in Theorem 2.4. These are statements about theories, not in the catalogue.

statement.name: Finite bound on n-types implies existence of a prime model
statement.definition: For complete T: if T has at most f(n) n-types for some function f, then T has a prime model.
statement.facts: Over RCA0 this implication implies ACA0.

statement.name: No complete theory has exactly two models up to isomorphism
statement.definition: There is no complete theory with exactly two models up to isomorphism.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 (Chang–Keisler Thm 2.3.15); implies WKL0 over RCA0 (Corollary 2.11(ii)).

statement.name: For every n ≥ 3 there is a complete theory with exactly n models
statement.definition: For every n ≥ 3 there is a complete theory T with exactly n models up to isomorphism.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0; over RCA0 it is implied by ¬WKL0 (Theorem 2.10, Corollary 2.11(i)). Theorem 2.10: in RCA0 + ¬WKL0, for every n ≥ 1 there is a complete theory with exactly n models (n=1 via Prop 3.5, n ≥ 2 via Millar's construction and an inseparable Σ01 pair).

statement.notation: finitely many models with a nonprincipal type
statement.name: Complete theory with a nonprincipal type (or infinitely many n-types) and finitely many models
statement.definition: (ii) There is a complete theory with a nonprincipal type and only finitely many models; (iii) a complete theory with infinitely many n-types for some n and only finitely many models.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, (i) (¬WKL0) ∨ ACA0, (ii) and (iii) are equivalent (Theorem 2.12); over WKL0, ACA0, (ii), (iii) are equivalent (Proposition 5.7). Their negation is equivalent to WKL0 + ¬ACA0. Question 2.13 on the values n possible in WKL0 + ¬ACA0 is open.

statement.name: Existence of an elementary-universal model of T implies finitely many n-types
statement.definition: A model A of T is elementary-universal if every model of T embeds elementarily into A.
statement.facts: WKL0 + ¬ACA0 proves ('T has an elementary-universal model' → S3) and (S4 → S3); hence WKL0 proves (S4 → S3) (Proposition 5.6).

statement.name: Σ01 separation principle in sentence form
statement.definition: There is no inseparable disjoint Σ01 pair: every disjoint pair of approximations ⟨Us,Vs⟩ has a separating set C with Us ⊆ C ⊆ M−Vs.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Lemma 7.2, from Simpson IV.4.4); recorded as the fact sep ↔ wkl, the sentence form being close to the catalogue problem sep.

statement.name: Eventually constant tails for trees
statement.definition: If f : 2^{<N} -> n then there is a node sigma such that for all tau, alpha extending sigma there is beta properly extending alpha with f(tau)=f(beta).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ECT(N) and to Sigma^0_2 induction over RCA0 (Lemmas 3, 4, 5, Theorem 6); implies TT(1) via the standard tree.

statement.name: Limit principles
statement.definition: L: given f : N^2 -> a such that lim_n f(x,n) exists for every x, there is a least b such that lim_n f(x,n)=b for some x. L+: the same with 'every' replaced by 'some' in the hypothesis.
statement.facts: Sigma^0_2 induction implies L+ implies L (Lemma 8); L implies TT(1) (Lemma 9); L and L+ are equivalent to Sigma^0_2 induction over RCA0 (Corollary 10).

statement.name: Existence of a node whose standard tree is isomorphic to 2^{<N}
statement.definition: If f : 2^{<N} -> a then there is a node sigma such that the standard tree of color f(sigma) based at sigma is isomorphic to 2^{<N}.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Sigma^0_2 induction over RCA0 (Theorem 11).

statement.name: Common zero node for null stable colorings
statement.definition: For every finite sequence of null stable colorings f_i : 2^{<N} -> 2 (above every node there is a node above which f_i is constantly 0) there is sigma with f_i(sigma)=0 for all i<n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Sigma^0_2 induction over RCA0 (Theorem 12).

statement.name: Simultaneous pigeonhole for trees
statement.definition: For each i<n and f_i : 2^{<N} -> 2 there is a subtree S isomorphic to 2^{<N} on which every f_i is constant (also restricted to null stable f_i).
statement.facts: Equivalent to TT(1) over RCA0, also in the restriction to null stable colorings (Theorem 13).

statement.name: Tree theorem for pairs restricted to 3-stable colorings
statement.definition: Every 3-stable 2-coloring of comparable pairs of 2^{<N} has a monochromatic subtree isomorphic to 2^{<N}; f is 3-stable if for each sigma there is c<k such that for every sigma' extending sigma there is tau properly extending sigma' with f(sigma,rho)=c for all rho extending tau.
statement.facts: Implies TT(1) over RCA0 (Theorem 14); open whether it implies Sigma^0_2 induction. It is a Pi^1_2 sentence. Possibly differs from the catalogue's stt22 (notion of stability).

statement.name: Domination problem (instance f in omega^omega, solution g dominating f)
statement.definition: Instance: a function f; solution: a function g with g >=* f. Different from the catalogue's DOM (instance a set C).
statement.facts: Cichon diagram of effective morphisms: Capture(M) -> Dom (Prop. 3.3), Dom -> Supset(M) (Prop. 3.6), Split -> Dom (Lemma 2.17), AEDiff -> Dom (Prop. 4.13), Dom -> Trace, Dom -> Supset(E) (Prop. 7.10); H(Dom) = high degrees, NL(Dom) = hyperimmune degrees.

statement.name: Escaping problem (dual of Dom)
statement.definition: Instance: a function g; solution: a function not dominated by g. NL(Esc) = high degrees, H(Esc) = hyperimmune degrees.
statement.facts: Esc -> Dom; Esc <-> EscDom (Lemma 7.17); Esc <-> GapEsc (Lemma 7.21); Esc -> Supset(E,N) (Prop. 7.14).

statement.name: Problems associated with the meagre ideal
statement.definition: Capture(M): given y find a Sigma^0_2 meagre set containing y; Pass(M): given a meagre set find a point outside it (H = weakly 1-generic); Supset(M): given a meagre set find a meagre superset; Spill(M): dual of Supset(M).
statement.facts: Capture(M) -> Dom (Prop. 3.3); Pass(M) -> Supset(M) (Prop. 3.4); Dom -> Supset(M) (Prop. 3.6); Capture(M) -> Pass(N) (Prop. 3.12); Supset(M) -> Pass(M)*Dom (Prop. 4.9); Supset(M) -> Supset(N) (Thm 3.18); Corollary 4.15: weakly meagre engulfing iff high or DNR; not low for meagre sets iff hyperimmune or DNR.

statement.name: Problems associated with the null ideal (Schnorr tests)
statement.definition: Same as for M with Pi^0_2 null sets given as Schnorr tests (with measures); H(Pass(N)) = oracles computing a Schnorr random.
statement.facts: Capture(N), Pass(N) -> Supset(N) (Prop. 3.9); Trace <-> Supset(N) (Thm 3.14); Cor. 3.16: strongly null engulfing iff high; Cor. 3.17: low for Schnorr tests iff computably traceable.

statement.name: Tracing problem
statement.definition: Instance: f in omega^omega; solution: an h-trace (slalom with |T(n)|<=h(n)) tracing f almost everywhere; equivalent for all order functions h (Lemma 3.13).
statement.facts: Dom -> Trace; H(Trace) = high degrees; NL(Trace) = not computably traceable; Trace <-> Trace^omega (Lemma 3.21); Supset(CND,M) -> Trace (Prop. 3.22).

statement.name: Infinitely often equal / almost everywhere different problems
statement.definition: AEDiff: given f find g eventually different from f; IOE is its dual: given g find f agreeing with g infinitely often.
statement.facts: NL(IOE) = high or DNR (Prop. 4.11, Kjos-Hanssen, Merkle, Stephan); Capture(M) -> AEDiff -> Dom (Props 4.12, 4.13); Pass(M) -> IOE*IOE (Prop. 4.14); Supset(E,N) <-> IOE (Prop. 7.8).

statement.name: Splitting problem
statement.definition: Instance: infinite subset a of omega; solution: infinite b splitting a. H(Split) = oracles computing a bi-immune set; NL(Split) = oracles computing r-cohesive sets.
statement.facts: Split -> Dom (Lemma 2.17): every high degree computes a bi-immune set; every r-cohesive set has hyperimmune degree.

statement.name: Problems for the ideal generated by compact null sets (Kurtz)
statement.definition: Supset(E): given a null Sigma^0_2 set find a null Sigma^0_2 superset; Supset(E,N): superset required only to be null.
statement.facts: Supset(E) <-> Supset(M) up to finite sequential composition (Thm 7.1); Thm 7.3: low for Sigma^0_2 null sets iff hyperimmune-free and not DNR; Thm 7.6 (Greenberg-Miller): low for Kurtz tests iff low for Kurtz randomness iff hyperimmune-free and not DNR.

statement.name: Besicovitch-distance and bounded IOE problems
statement.definition: Close(p): given x find y with Besicovitch distance < p; Far(p) its dual; IOE(h) is IOE restricted to functions bounded by h.
statement.facts: Theorem 6.15 (Monin-Nies): for computable p in (1/2,1), Far(p) is equivalent (in the weakened morphism order) to IOE(2^{2^n}); yields Monin's theorem 6.16 (Gamma(d)<1/2 implies Gamma(d)=0).

statement.notation: B(·)H(·)G(·)-M (24 variants, e.g. B′′H′G′′-M, B′H′′G′-M, BH′′G′′-M)
statement.name: Marriage theorems with smallness and Hall conditions
statement.definition: If a bipartite graph R(B,G) satisfies the smallness conditions on boys (none, locally finite B′, highly recursive B′′) and girls (G, G′, G′′) and a Hall condition (H, expanding H′, computable expanding H′′), then it has an injective selection (matching).
statement.facts: Table 1, Theorems 2.13 and 2.15: variants with B′′ (boys highly recursive) are equivalent to WKL over RCA0 (Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.4, Hirst); variants with B′ or B (not B′′) and not G′′+H′′ are equivalent to ACA over RCA0 (Lemma 2.3, Lemma 2.6, Proposition 2.14); B′′H′′G′′-M is provable in RCA0 (Kierstead) and BH′′G′′-M in RCA0 + Σ03-IND (Theorem 2.7). Theorem 4.2: Weihrauch degrees KL, Lim_{N^N}, WKL, id for the respective groups.

statement.notation: B′H_cb G-M etc. (constant bounded Hall condition H_cb)
statement.name: Marriage theorems with constant bounded Hall condition
statement.definition: There is k such that |X| ≤ |R[X]| ≤ |X|+k for all finite X ⊆ B.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.1: B′H_cb G-M provable in RCA0. Theorem 4.3: B′H_cb G-M and B′H_cb G′-M are Weihrauch equivalent to Lim_N; B′H_cb G′′-M and B′′H_cb G′′-M to id. Theorem 4.4: WKL_{<ω} ≤W B′′H_cb G′-M ≤W B′′H_cb G-M ≤W inf(Lim_N, WKL).

statement.name: Sequential version of a marriage theorem
statement.definition: Sequential version: for every sequence of instances there is a sequence of solutions.
statement.facts: Theorems 3.2, 3.3: Seq(B′H_cb G-M), Seq(B′H_cb G′-M) equivalent to ACA over RCA0; Seq(B′′H_cb G-M), Seq(B′′H_cb G′-M) equivalent to WKL over RCA0 (Theorem 3.3); Seq(B′H_cb G′′-M) and Seq(B′′H_cb G′′-M) provable in RCA0 (Theorem 3.5, Corollary 3.7).

statement.notation: WKL_{<ω}, WKL_n (with a star/question mark lost in extraction)
statement.name: Weak König lemma for trees with finitely many branching nodes
statement.definition: WKL restricted to infinite binary trees with finitely many (resp. fewer than n) branching nodes.
statement.facts: LLPO ≤W WKL_2; every WKL_n is reducible to an iterated use of LLPO; Theorem 4.4: WKL_{<ω} ≤W B′′H_cb G′-M.

statement.name: Dependent choice for disjunctions of simply universal assertions
statement.loc: Section 2 (definition of DC-or) and Section 6, Theorem 26
statement.definition: DC-or: for all u (A0(u) or A1(u)) implies there is a binary sequence alpha with A_{alpha(n)}(alpha|n) for all n; Pi01-DC-or restricts to simply universal A0, A1 (Pi01 assertions).
statement.facts: Theorem 26: WKL implies Pi01-DC-or. Theorem 27 / Corollary 28: WKL is equivalent to LLPO + Pi01-DC-or (unwinding of [15, 16.5], without coding). Corollary 2: Gamma-DC-or implies Gamma-CC-or for Gamma = Delta0, Sigma01, Pi01; Corollary 5: converse. Proposition 3: Delta0-DC-or and Delta0-CC-or provable.

statement.name: Countable choice and dependent choice for disjunctions
statement.definition: CC-or: for all n (A0(n) or A1(n)) implies there is alpha with A_{alpha(n)}(n) for all n. DC-or as above.
statement.facts: Proposition 1: DC-or implies CC-or. Proposition 4: CC-or implies DC-or (using CODE and Delta0-DC-or).

statement.name: 1-Kőnig
statement.definition: For decidable D0, D1: for all n0 n1 (D0(n0) or D1(n1)) implies (for all n0 D0(n0)) or (for all n1 D1(n1)).
statement.facts: Proposition 21: LLPO and 1-Kőnig are equivalent (LLPO to 1-Kőnig indicated in Akama et al.).

statement.name: Weak spread lemma
statement.definition: Every spread (tree in which every node has an immediate successor in the tree) has an infinite path.
statement.facts: WKL implies WSL; Proposition 29: WSL is provable constructively; WSL is equivalent to Delta0-DC-or.

statement.name: Contrapositives of WKL and FAN
statement.definition: WKL': if a tree has no infinite path, then it is not infinite. FAN': if a tree is infinite, then it is not well-founded.
statement.facts: Corollary 12: WKL' + MP, FAN + MP and FAN' + MP are equivalent, and equivalent to: if a tree has no infinite path then it is finite. Proposition 14: WKL iff WKL' + (§); WKL' iff FAN' + (flat); WKL iff FAN' + (dagger). Corollary 15: WKL iff FAN + (dagger); under (dagger), WKL, WKL', FAN', FAN are equivalent.

statement.notation: tree-forms of LPO, WLPO, MP, LLPO, WLLPO
statement.name: Omniscience principles for binary trees
statement.definition: LPO: every tree is finite or infinite. WLPO: every tree is infinite or not infinite. MP: if a tree is not infinite it is finite; equivalently (*): a tree with no infinite path is well-founded. LLPO: T infinite implies T0 infinite or T1 infinite.
statement.facts: Proposition 8 (items 1-3), Proposition 10 (MP iff (*)), Proposition 19 (LLPO iff (3)); WLLPO restated as WLLPO0 equivalent (Lemma 22) and equivalent to Proposition 24 variants; MP equivalent to variants in Proposition 25.

statement.name: Uniform formulation of omniscience principles
statement.definition: P(Gamma, Delta): (C implies D) implies (not C or D) for C in Gamma, D in Delta; Gamma-LEM, Gamma-DML restrictions of excluded middle and De Morgan.
statement.facts: LPO, WLPO, LLPO, WLLPO are Sigma01-LEM, Pi01-LEM, Sigma01-DML, Pi01-DML; LLPO iff P(Sigma01, Pi01); WLLPO iff P(Pi01, Xi01); WLPO iff P(Sigma01, Psi) iff P(Sigma01, Xi01).

statement.name: Existence of the set of indices of graphs having a domatic 3-partition
statement.definition: For every sequence of graphs <G_i : i in N> there is a set Z such that for all i, i in Z iff G_i has a domatic 3-partition (a function f: V -> 3 such that every vertex is adjacent to a vertex of each other class, all classes nonempty, Definition 2.3).
statement.facts: Corollary 5.2: over RCA0 this is equivalent to Pi^1_1 comprehension (pi11ca). Proved from Simpson's Theorem 5.1 (Lemma VI.1.1) via the tree-to-graph construction of Theorem 4.5; the paper only sketches the derivation. Analogue of Gasarch-Hirst Theorem 20 for Hamilton paths.

statement.name: Existence of the set of indices of trees having a path
statement.definition: For any sequence of trees <T_k : k in N>, T_k subset of N^{<N}, there exists a set X such that for all k, k in X iff T_k has a path.
statement.facts: Cited from Simpson [9]: equivalent to Pi^1_1 comprehension (pi11ca) over RCA0.

statement.name: Complete Σ⁰_{k+1}-computable function on Baire space (Tarski–Kuratowski)
statement.definition: C_k(p)(n) = 0 iff (exists n_k)(forall n_{k-1})... <p<n,n_1,...,n_k>> = 0, else 1; the map NN -> NN.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.5: F <=_c C_k iff F is Sigma^0_{k+1}-computable (and <=_t iff measurable); Theorem 7.6 extends this to functions on computable metric spaces under realizer reducibility. Lemma 5.9: C_{k+1} = C_1 o F_k. Proposition 8.5: C_1 <=_c c_{k+1} <_c C_{k+1}.

statement.name: Characteristic function of a Wadge-complete Sigma^0_k set (small counterpart of C_k)
statement.definition: c_k(p) = 0 iff (exists n_k)(forall n_{k-1})... <p<n_1,...,n_k>> = 0, else 1; a point (0 or 1), corresponds to LPO-type principles in constructive mathematics.
statement.facts: Sigma^0_{k+1}-computable; Proposition 8.5: C_1 <=_c c_{k+1} <_c C_{k+1} and C_k <_c (C_k, c_{k+1}) <_c C_{k+1}. Remark after Prop. 8.5: the c_k correspond to the LPO-principles of constructive mathematics.

statement.name: Strong computable type problem of a compact pair (X, A)
statement.definition: For a compact pair (X, A) (compact metrizable X with compact A subset of X) in the Hilbert cube Q: the function taking a copy (Y, B) of (X, A) in Q, given in the upper Vietoris topology (i.e. as a semicomputable pair), and outputting Y in the Vietoris topology (i.e. as a computable compact set). Measures the non-uniformity of 'semicomputable implies computable'.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.4.1: if X is not a singleton, C_N <=^t_sW SCT_(X,A) (strong Weihrauch reducibility relative to some oracle), and C_N <=_sW SCT_(X,A) if (X,A) has a semicomputable copy. Theorem 4.4.2: if (X,A) is minimal for some Sigma^0_2 invariant (in the upper Vietoris topology) then SCT_(X,A) <=_W C_N. Whether SCT_(X,A) <=_W C_N for every pair with strong computable type is left open (Question 6.8.2, stated in the other part). Remark in the text: sW reduction SCT <=_sW C_N is impossible since C_N has countably many possible outputs while SCT has uncountably many. The paper's C_N is closed choice on N (Definition 4.4.5), matching catalogue cn, but SCT is not in the catalogue so no fact is entered.

statement.name: Maximum of a finite subset of N
statement.loc: Proof of Theorem 4.4.1 (cited from Brattka-Gherardi-Pauly [15], Theorem 7.13)
statement.definition: The problem sending a non-empty finite subset of N, represented by its characteristic function, to its maximal element.
statement.facts: Cited: Max is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to C_N (Theorem 7.13 of [15], used in the proof of Theorem 4.4.1). Max is not in the catalogue.

statement.name: Order types of countable ordered groups (Mal'tsev)
statement.definition: Every countable (fully) ordered group G has order type Z^alpha Q^epsilon for some well order alpha and epsilon in {0,1}.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to Pi11-CA0 (Theorem 3.6), and so is its restriction to ordered abelian groups (statement (3)); Lemma 4.9: the abelian version implies ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Order types of countable ordered abelian groups
statement.definition: Every countable ordered abelian group has order type Z^alpha Q^epsilon for a well order alpha and epsilon in {0,1}.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.6); implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Lemma 4.9) and the existence of W(X) for every linear order (Proposition 4.4).

statement.name: Existence of the well ordered initial segment of every linear order
statement.definition: For every linear order X, the set W(X) of elements x with no infinite descending sequence starting at x exists.
statement.facts: Provable in Pi11-CA0; implied over RCA0 by Mal'tsev's theorem for abelian ordered groups (Proposition 4.4).

statement.name: Path-existence set for a sequence of trees
statement.definition: For any sequence of trees <T_k>, there is a set X such that k in X iff T_k has a path.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Pi11-CA0 over RCA0 (cited from Simpson 1999).

statement.name: Strong comparison of well orders implies alpha+1 <=s beta
statement.definition: If alpha, beta are well orders with alpha <=s beta and beta not <=s alpha then alpha+1 <=s beta.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Hirst 1999, cited).

statement.name: Eulerian path with prescribed start vertex (undirected, directed)
statement.definition: Input (G, v) with G a countable (directed) graph having a one-way Eulerian path starting from v; output such a path starting from v.
statement.facts: EPstart ≡W DEPstart ≡W lim (Theorem 3.2).

statement.notation: EP restricted to locally finite graphs
statement.name: One-way Eulerian paths in locally finite graphs
statement.definition: The restriction of EP to locally finite graphs.
statement.facts: Weihrauch equivalent to lim (Corollary 2.6); the directed version too (remark after the corollary).

statement.name: Degree function of a graph vertex (general, locally finite)
statement.definition: Deg takes a graph G and a vertex v and returns deg_G(v) in N ∪ {∞}; DegLF is its restriction to locally finite graphs.
statement.facts: DegLF ≡W C_N <W Deg ≡W sTC_N (Proposition 2.5).

statement.name: Orienting the edges of a graph with a two-way Eulerian path
statement.definition: Given an undirected graph G in dom(EP2), return an orientation D in dom(DEP2) (the map (v,w) -> {v,w} a computable bijection from arcs onto edges).
statement.facts: OrientEP2 is computable (Theorem 5.6).

statement.name: Limit on the natural numbers
statement.definition: limit of a convergent sequence in the discrete space N.
statement.facts: lim_2 <W lim_N <W lim and C_N ≡W lim_N, cited from [4] and [5].

statement.name: Bounded monotone enumeration principle
statement.definition: For M0 a model of RCA0 + BΣ^0_2: for every b, every Σ^0_1 relation P(E,E′) with parameters whose image sets P′(E) are M0-finite, and every M0-finite E, there is s* such that the union over v ≤ b of P^v_s(E) stabilises for s > s* (so the union of the iterates P^v(E), v ≤ b, is M0-finite).
statement.facts: Fails in some models of BΣ^0_2 + ¬IΣ^0_2; follows from IΣ^0_2; is a Π^0_3 sentence; equivalent over RCA0 to PΣ^0_1 and to totality of the Ackermann function (Kreuzer and Yokoyama [26]); RCA0 + BME1 + BΣ^0_2 is the ground-model setting for the proof of Theorem 3.2; RCA0 does not prove BME1 (Remark 3.7); TT^1 is Π^1_1-conservative over BME1 + BΣ^0_2 (Chong, Li, Wang and Yang [8]).

statement.name: Weak König's lemma with the hypothesis that any two infinite paths agree
statement.definition: For a detachable subtree of the binary fan coded by rho: if for every y there is a binary sequence alpha with rho(alpha(x)) = 0 for all x <= y, and any two infinite paths alpha, beta (forall x rho(alpha(x))=0 and rho(beta(x))=0) are equal, then there is an infinite path. Obtained from WKL by adding the hypothesis that any two paths agree; weaker uniqueness hypothesis than WKL!.
statement.facts: WKL constructively entails WKL!!, and WKL!! constructively entails WKL! and hence FTd (Section 3). WKL!! entails MP∨ (Theorem 3) and ¬¬WKL (Theorem 4, provable in M); conversely WKL!! is a constructive consequence of MP∨ + ¬¬WKL (Theorem 5), so WKL!! is interderivable over M with MP∨ + ¬¬WKL (Section 4). M + FTd does not prove WKL!! (Corollary 6, via G realizability and the non-realizability of MP∨), so WKL!! is not a consequence of WKL! or FTd; M + WKL!! does not prove WKL (Corollary 7, via Kleene function realizability). So WKL!! lies strictly between WKL! and WKL.

statement.name: Double negation of weak König's lemma
statement.definition: The double negation of the open axiom WKL: forall y exists alpha in 2^N forall x <= y rho(alpha(x)) = 0 implies not not exists alpha in 2^N forall x rho(alpha(x)) = 0.
statement.facts: WKL!! -> ¬¬WKL is provable in M (Theorem 4); WKL!! is a constructive consequence of MP∨ and ¬¬WKL (Theorem 5).

statement.name: Separation principle for detachable bars
statement.definition: For all alpha, beta in 2^N, if exists x rho(alpha(x)) != 0 or exists x sigma(beta(x)) != 0 (for all alpha, beta), then either every alpha in 2^N has an x with rho(alpha(x)) != 0, or every beta in 2^N has an x with sigma(beta(x)) != 0.
statement.facts: FTd constructively entails SP (Lemma 1); SP is used in the proof that FTd entails WKL! (Proposition 2).

statement.name: Full fan theorem
statement.definition: For all R, if for every alpha in 2^N there is x with R(alpha(x)), then there is y such that for every alpha in 2^N there is x <= y with R(alpha(x)); no restriction on the predicate R.
statement.facts: Accepted in intuitionistic mathematics; classically (not constructively) FT and FTd are interderivable with the restriction KL of König's lemma to the binary fan.

statement.name: Sorting infinite sequences over an alphabet of size d
statement.definition: Sort_d : d^omega -> d^omega maps p to 0^{c_0} 1^{c_1} ... k^infinity, where c_i is the number of occurrences of i in p and k is the least letter occurring infinitely often. Sort = Sort_2.
statement.facts: XC_n <=W Sort_{n+1} (Theorem 18); Sort_{k+1} is not <=W Sort_k (Corollary 17, alternative proof of a result of Neumann and Pauly); C_{#<=k+1} is not <=W Sort_k (Theorem 20); C_2 x f <=W Sort_{k+1} implies f <=W Sort_k x C_N (Proposition 13); Sort_{n+1} equivalent to a finite product of Sort (from Pauly and Tsuiki) and Sort^* equivalent to the coproduct of the Sort_d (Section 3).

statement.name: Closed choice for convex sets in [0,1]^n (convex choice in dimension n)
statement.definition: The restriction of C_{[0,1]^n} to convex closed sets. XC_1 is interval choice C_I (connected choice CC_1).
statement.facts: XC_n <=W Sort_{n+1} (Theorem 18); XC_2 restricted to closed triangles is not <=W XC_1 x XC_1 (Theorem 28); XC_1 * AoUC is not <=W XC_k for any k (Theorem 32); C_2 x XC_1^n is not <=W Sort_{n+1} (Corollary 16); C_2 x AoUC is not <=W XC_1 (Theorem 12).

statement.name: Finite choice with exactly n, respectively at most n, elements
statement.definition: C_{X,#=n} is closed choice on X restricted to closed sets with exactly n points, C_{X,#<=n} restricted to sets with between 1 and n points; for computably compact computably rich X they are equivalent to the versions on {0,1}^N (Le Roux and Pauly).
statement.facts: C_{#<=k+1} is not <=W Sort_k (Theorem 20); C_{#<=k} <=W C_{#<=n_0} x ... x C_{#<=n_l} iff Player 2 wins the comparison game (Theorem 24); the comparison game with all n_i = 2 is won by Player 2 if k+1 <= l and by Player 1 if k+1 >= 2^l - 1 (Proposition 25, the exact bound in the extracted text is unclear).

statement.name: Finding a connected component of a countable graph with finitely many components (with a bound on their number)
statement.definition: Given the characteristic functions of V and E and a bound on the number of connected components, produce the characteristic function of a connected component. Studied in reverse mathematics by Gura, Hirst and Mummert, where it is equivalent to Sigma^0_2 induction.
statement.facts: FCC is Weihrauch equivalent to Sort^*, the finite parallelization of Sort, and FCC x FCC <=W FCC (Theorem 19).

statement.notation: *RCA0' (BNA + STP + Special Sigma^S_1 Induction + Special Delta^S_1 Comprehension)
statement.name: Nonstandard counterpart of RCA0 with the full Standard Part Principle
statement.definition: Theory in the language L2 + *L1 (standard integers, hyperintegers, sets coded by prime divisors) with the axioms of BNA, Special Sigma^S_1 Induction, Special Delta^S_1 Comprehension and the Standard Part Principle STP (every set is coded by a hyperinteger and conversely).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.4: *RCA0' implies RCA0. Theorem 3.5: *RCA0' + forall-Transfer is conservative over RCA0 (every L2 sentence provable is provable in RCA0). Proposition 3.3: *WKL0 implies *RCA0'. Proposition 6.7: Downward Shadow Principle is provable in *RCA0' + forall-T. Proposition 6.9: the Upward Shadow Principle is not provable in *RCA0' + forall-T.

statement.name: Basic Nonstandard Arithmetic
statement.definition: Axioms of IΣ1 in L1, < a strict linear order, and the Proper Initial Segment Axioms in the two-sorted language *L1.
statement.facts: BNA + STP alone says little about sets: it does not even imply the existence of infinite sets (Section 3 remark).

statement.notation: Overspill, Internal Induction, Transfer for Pi^0_1 sentences (over T0 = RCA0 + BNA + STP)
statement.name: Nonstandard principles in the language *L1
statement.definition: Transfer for Pi^0_1 sentences; Internal Induction for Delta^S_0 formulas; Overspill for Delta^S_0 formulas.
statement.facts: Proposition 6.11: over T0, Transfer for Pi^0_1 sentences implies Internal Induction, which implies Overspill, which implies WKL0. Hence *RCA0' plus any of them is not conservative over RCA0.

statement.name: Delta^S_0 comprehension in nonstandard arithmetic
statement.definition: Scheme: exists z forall m [(p_m | z) <-> phi(m, u)] for Delta^S_0 formulas phi.
statement.facts: Proposition 6.14: T1 implies WKL0; any model of T1 where Overspill fails satisfies S-ACA and ACA0.

statement.name: Nonstandard arithmetic with primitive recursive function symbols
statement.definition: RCA0 with symbols for all primitive recursive functions, Transfer for universal sentences of L1(PR), BNA and STP.
statement.facts: Proposition 6.17: it implies Overspill and WKL0, so it is not conservative over RCA0 (Remark 6.18: it is conservative over WKL0).

statement.notation: Every torsion free abelian group is an O-group
statement.name: Orderability of torsion free abelian groups
statement.definition: Every torsion free abelian group admits a full (linear, translation invariant) order.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3 (Hatzikiriakou and Simpson 1990, cited): equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.notation: Every torsion free nilpotent group is an O-group
statement.name: Orderability of torsion free nilpotent groups
statement.definition: Every torsion free nilpotent group (given with a code for its upper central series) is fully orderable.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.12: equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Restricted countable direct product of O-groups is an O-group
statement.definition: If every Ai of a sequence of groups is fully orderable, the restricted direct product of the Ai is fully orderable.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.6: equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0. Theorem 4.3: provable in RCA0 for finite products.

statement.name: Every group has a center
statement.definition: For every group G the set C(G) = {g : forall x (gx = xg)} exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0, already for 2 step nilpotent groups (free 2 step nilpotent group construction).

statement.name: Existence of the induced order on a quotient of a p.o. group by a convex normal subgroup
statement.definition: For every partially ordered group (G, <=) and convex normal subgroup H, the induced order on G/H exists.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.18: equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0. Theorem 2.14: for fully ordered groups it is provable in RCA0.

statement.name: Fuchs, Los-Ohnishi and Lorenzen semigroup conditions for full orderability
statement.definition: Equations (2), (3), (4): conditions on normal semigroups generated by sequences of elements characterizing extendability of a partial order to a full order, and full orderability.
statement.facts: Each is provable in WKL0 and each is equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.10).

statement.name: Archimedean fully ordered groups embed in (R,+)
statement.definition: Every nontrivial Archimedean fully ordered group is order isomorphic to a nontrivial subgroup of the additive reals.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0.

statement.notation: Unique divisible closure of an abelian group
statement.name: Uniqueness of divisible closures
statement.definition: Every abelian group has a unique divisible closure.
statement.facts: Theorem 8.4 (Friedman, Simpson and Smith 1983, cited): existence of a divisible closure is provable in RCA0; uniqueness is equivalent to ACA0.

statement.name: Existence of strong divisible closures (also f.o. version for Archimedean groups)
statement.definition: Every abelian group has a divisible closure h: A -> D which is an isomorphism of A onto a subgroup of D (a strong divisible closure); for Archimedean fully ordered groups, an order preserving one.
statement.facts: Theorem 8.7: both versions are equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Canonical Ramsey theorem for exponent n
statement.definition: Every f : [N]^n → N has a canonical set, i.e. an infinite C and u ⊆ n with f(x1) = f(x2) iff x1|u = x2|u for x1, x2 in [C]^n (Definition 1.6).
statement.facts: Over RCA0, CRT^n is equivalent to ACA0 for each fixed n ≥ 2 (Proposition 8.2) and CRT^1 is equivalent to BΣ^0_2 (Proposition 8.5); computable instances have Π^0_{2n-2} canonical sets (Theorem 5.5), and for n = 2 sharp (no Σ^0_2); upper Turing bound a ≫ 0^(2n-3) for n ≥ 2 (Theorem 4.5), conjectured sharp for n ≥ 3 (Conjectures 7.15, 7.16). Only n = 2 (canrt2) is in the catalogue.

statement.name: Canonical Ramsey theorem (all exponents)
statement.definition: For all n ≥ 1, every f : [N]^n → N has a canonical set.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to ACA0' (all finite jumps), REG and RT (Proposition 8.4).

statement.name: Regressive function theorem for exponent n (Kanamori–McAloon)
statement.definition: Every regressive f : [N]^n → N has a minhomogeneous set M (infinite, f(x) = f(y) for x, y in [M]^n with min x = min y).
statement.facts: Over RCA0, REG^n is equivalent to ACA0 for each fixed n ≥ 2 (Proposition 8.2); computable regressive instances have Π^0_n minhomogeneous sets (Theorem 6.6) and Turing bound a ≫ 0^(n-1) (Theorem 6.5), both sharp (Theorem 7.6, Corollaries 7.7, 7.9). Only n = 2 (regrt2) is in the catalogue.

statement.name: Regressive function theorem (all exponents)
statement.definition: For all n ≥ 1, every regressive f : [N]^n → N has a minhomogeneous set.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to ACA0', CRT and RT (Proposition 8.4).

statement.name: Minhomogeneous sets for h-regressive functions
statement.definition: For h : ω → ω, f is h-regressive if f(x) < h(min x) when h(min x) > 0; every such f : [N]^2 → N has a minhomogeneous set.
statement.facts: Hirst (thesis): this statement implies ACA0 over RCA0 (stated in Remark 8.3, cited). Not entered since the statement is not in the catalogue.

statement.name: Complete choice principle for the class Λ2,3
statement.loc: Section 3.2.6, A complete choice principle for Λ2,3
statement.definition: C_{2,3}(x) = lim_n (skip0[(info(x))_n] - 1): from x take the unique component (x)_n carrying infinitely many nonzero entries, extract it as a sequence of finite words, and take the limit of this sequence (domain: such x for which the limit exists).
statement.facts: Proposition 3.65: C_{2,3} is in Λ2,3. Theorem 3.66: a function f between represented spaces is Λ2,3 iff f ≤t C_{2,3} (Weihrauch complete for Λ2,3), proved from Semmes's game G_{2,3}.

statement.name: Complete choice principle for the class Λ3,3
statement.loc: Section 3.2.6, A complete choice principle for Λ3,3
statement.definition: C_{3,3}(x) = skip0(info(x)) - 1 with domain the x for which exactly one component (x)_n has infinitely many nonzero entries: decode the unique sequence encoded by x that contains infinite information.
statement.facts: Proposition 3.67: C_{3,3} is in Λ3,3. Theorem 3.68: f is Λ3,3 iff f ≤t C_{3,3} (Weihrauch complete for Λ3,3, the functions preserving Δ⁰₃ under preimages), via the multitape game.

statement.name: Continuous choice (the flip function)
statement.definition: C_0(x)(n) = 0 if x(n) ≠ 0 and 1 otherwise: a continuous function flipping nonzero values to 0 and 0 to 1.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.45: f is continuous iff f ≤t C_0 (Weihrauch complete for the continuous functions).

statement.name: k-countable choice
statement.definition: C_k(x)(n) = 0 iff ∃n_{k-1} ∀n_{k-2} ... Q n_0 x(⟨n, n_{k-1}, ..., n_0⟩) ≠ 0 (alternating quantifiers), and 1 otherwise; C_1 is countable choice C.
statement.facts: Proposition 3.60: C_k is of Baire class k. Theorem 3.61 (cited from Brattka 2005): f ∈ Λ1,k+1 iff f ≤t C_k, so C_k is Weihrauch complete for the Baire class k functions.

statement.name: Discrete choice on omega
statement.definition: C_ω(x) = ω \ ran x with domain {x : ran x ≠ ω}: given a sequence omitting some natural number, return a number outside its range. Closely related to the catalogue's C_N (closed choice on N), but coded without a placeholder for the empty enumeration.
statement.facts: Proposition 3.47: C_ω ∈ Λ2,2. Theorem 3.48 (Brattka, de Brecht, Pauly): f ∈ Λ2,2 iff f ≤t C_ω, with a new game proof (backtrack game). Proposition 3.49: lim_Δ ≤t C_ω, where lim_Δ is the discrete limit representation.

statement.name: Infinite stable marriage theorem (all preferences of order type omega, N-listed)
statement.definition: Infinite instance with countably many boys and girls, uniformly recursive preference orders all of order type omega; a stable matching has no blocking pair and one side is fully matched.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 2.6); every such instance has a stable matching by infinite Gale-Shapley algorithm (Theorem 2.1, not formalized).

statement.notation: stable marriage with levels / ordered stable marriage
statement.name: Stable marriage for well-ordered preferences
statement.definition: Instances with preferences given by well-orderings (ordered: all boys share one well-order of girls and all girls one of boys; with levels: blockwise order type omega).
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to ATR0 (Theorem 2.7), via CWO.

statement.name: Stable marriage with bounded instances (domain B / symmetric solutions)
statement.definition: Conditions 1(a), 1(b): each boy (girl) lies in a finite set of n boys that are the n first choices of n girls (dually).
statement.facts: Over RCA0, ACA0 is equivalent to existence of a solution with domain B for B-bounded N-listed problems and to symmetric solutions for bounded N-listed problems.

statement.notation: highly B-bounded / highly bounded effectively N-listed stable marriage
statement.name: Stable marriage with effective bounds
statement.definition: Bounded instances where the finite witness sets are computable from b, g and preference lists are effectively listed.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to WKL0 (Theorem 2.9), using bounded Konig lemma and Sigma^0_1 separation.

statement.name: Perfect matching in highly recursive degree-2 societies
statement.definition: Degree <= 2 society S = (B, G, K) with functions K_B, K_G listing who each boy/girl knows; find a bijection M: B -> G within K.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to WKL0 (Theorem 3.2); instances have finitely many or 2^aleph0 solutions (Theorem 3.1).

statement.notation: Dilworth's theorem (width k covered by k chains)
statement.name: Dilworth's theorem for infinite posets
statement.definition: Any poset of width k can be covered by k chains.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to WKL0. Not the chain-antichain principle CAC.

statement.notation: Dual Dilworth (height k covered by k antichains)
statement.name: Dual Dilworth theorem for infinite posets
statement.definition: Any poset of height k can be covered by k antichains.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to WKL0.

statement.notation: Local dimension <= d implies dimension <= d
statement.name: Dimension of posets from local dimension
statement.definition: Every poset (N, <=_A) such that each restriction to {0..n} has dimension <= d has dimension <= d.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, equivalent to WKL0.

statement.name: n-Ramsey property of a partial ordering P
statement.definition: For a partial ordering P, R^k_n(P) says that for every coloring of the n-element chains of P in k colors there is a monochromatic subordering of P isomorphic to P; R_n(P) means R^k_n(P) for all k. For P = omega this is Ramsey's theorem for n-tuples.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, for standard n >= 3, ACA0 is equivalent to: omega is n-Ramsey; every bounded-level proto-Ramsey j.e.p. edge-Ramsey partial ordering is n-Ramsey; there is an infinite bounded-level n-Ramsey partial ordering with least element (Theorem 4.1). Theorem 5.1: there is a primitive recursive partial ordering P (the complete omega-branching tree with extra left connections, Definition 5.2) such that over RCA0, R^2_2(P) is equivalent to ACA0 (Propositions 5.9 and 5.10). Theorem 2.14 (RCA0): a 3-Ramsey bounded-level partial ordering with least element is biembeddable with a weakly proto-Ramsey one; Theorem 2.27: for weakly proto-Ramsey P, 2-Ramsey implies G(P) edge-Ramsey with joint embedding; Theorem 3.1 (ATR0): bounded-level weakly proto-Ramsey 2-Ramsey implies biembeddable with a proto-Ramsey ordering.

statement.notation: Torsion free abelian groups are O-groups
statement.name: Orderability of torsion free abelian groups
statement.definition: Every torsion free abelian group admits a full order.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Hatzikiriakou and Simpson 1990, cited in Section 4).

statement.notation: Torsion free nilpotent groups are O-groups
statement.name: Orderability of torsion free nilpotent groups
statement.definition: Every torsion free nilpotent group (given by a code with explicit upper central series) is an O-group.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.5).

statement.name: Countable direct product of O-groups is an O-group
statement.definition: If every Ai is an O-group then the direct product of the Ai, i in N, is an O-group.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.6).

statement.name: Existence of the center of a group
statement.definition: For each group G, the center C(G) exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.2).

statement.notation: Induced order on G/H for p.o. groups
statement.name: Existence of the induced order on a quotient of a partially ordered group by a convex normal subgroup
statement.definition: For every p.o. group and every convex normal subgroup H, the induced order on G/H exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.9); for f.o. groups it is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 3.8).

statement.notation: Free group on two generators is an O-group
statement.name: Orderability of free groups
statement.definition: The free group on two (or countably many) generators is an O-group.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0.

statement.notation: Every ordered group is the o-epimorphic image of an ordered free group
statement.name: Ordered groups as images of ordered free groups
statement.definition: Any ordered group is the order preserving epimorphic image of an ordered free group.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0.

statement.name: Hölder's Theorem
statement.definition: Every Archimedean ordered group is order isomorphic to a subgroup of (R,+).
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0.

statement.notation: Mal'tsev's classification of order types of countable ordered groups
statement.name: Mal'tsev's theorem
statement.definition: Every countable (abelian) ordered group has order type Z^alpha Q^epsilon for a well order alpha and epsilon = 0 or 1.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.3), for general and for abelian groups.

statement.name: Existence of strong divisible closures of abelian groups
statement.definition: Every abelian group (equivalently every Archimedean ordered group) has a strong divisible closure.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 7.8). Related: every abelian group has a divisible closure (RCA0, Theorem 7.5(1)); unique divisible closure is equivalent to ACA0 (7.5(2)); for ordered abelian groups existence and uniqueness of ordered divisible closure is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 7.6, Downey-Kurtz).

statement.name: Existence of strong real closures of ordered fields
statement.definition: Every countable ordered field has a strong real closure.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Friedman, Simpson and Smith 1983); existence and uniqueness of real closures provable in RCA0 (7.2(1),(2)).

statement.notation: Every countable field has an algebraic closure
statement.name: Existence of algebraic closures
statement.definition: Every countable field has an algebraic closure.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Friedman, Simpson and Smith 1983).

statement.name: Theorems of Fuchs, Los-Ohnishi and Lorenzen on extending orders
statement.definition: Conditions on normal semigroups S(a1^e1,...,an^en) characterising extendability of partial orders and O-groups.
statement.facts: Stated to be equivalent to WKL0 (in the formulation with the function s(A,n,m,x)), Section 4 before Theorem 4.7.

statement.name: Clopen Lipschitz determinacy
statement.definition: Determinacy of Lipschitz games G_L(A,B) in the Baire space where A,B are Δ01 (both Σ01 and Π01 equivalent) payoff sets; player II wins iff A(f) <-> B(g).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over ACA0 (Theorem 2), and to Δ01-SLOL; ATR0 proves it (Section 3.2).

statement.name: Clopen Semi-Linear Ordering principle (Lipschitz)
statement.definition: For clopen A,B in the Baire space, Red_L(A,B) or Red_L(not B, A): A Lipschitz reduces to B or the complement of B Lipschitz reduces to A.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 and to Δ01-DetL over ACA0 (Theorem 2); implied by Δ01-DetL over RCA0 (Lemma 1).
