statement.name: Closed Lipschitz determinacy
statement.definition: Determinacy of Lipschitz games G_L(A,B) with A,B Π01 (closed sets of the Baire space).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5), also to (Δ01,Π01)-DetL and (Δ01,Σ01∧Π01)-SLOL; ATR0 proves Π01-DetL and (Δ01,Σ01∧Π01)-DetL (Proposition 3).

statement.name: Lipschitz determinacy with clopen and closed payoffs
statement.definition: Determinacy of G_L(A,B) with A Δ01 and B Π01.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5); it implies ACA0 over RCA0 (proof of (3)=>(1)).

statement.name: Lipschitz semilinear ordering for clopen and difference-of-open sets
statement.definition: Red_L(A,B) or Red_L(not B,A) for A in Δ01 and B in Σ01∧Π01.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5); implies ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Weak comparability of countable well orderings
statement.definition: For all countable well orderings α,β there is an order-preserving injection of one into the other (α ≤w β or β ≤w α).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3, cited from Hirst, Theorem 4 of [5]).

statement.name: Existence of rank functions for well-founded trees
statement.definition: Every well-founded tree T in N^{<N} has a rank function (rk, α) with α a countable well ordering.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4, essentially Theorem 7 of Hirst [4]).

statement.name: Nonstandard counterpart of WWKL0
statement.definition: System of nonstandard second-order arithmetic: ns-BASIC (standard part RCA0, embedding and end extension principles, Sigma^0_1 overspill, Sigma^0_1/Sigma^1_0 equivalence, Delta^0_0 transfer) plus the Loeb measure property LMP (if a nonstandard tree has positive Loeb measure, its standard part has a path).
statement.facts: ns-WWKL0 proves WWKL in the standard universe (Theorem 3.4) and is a conservative extension of WWKL0 (Theorem 3.5). LMP is equivalent over ns-BASIC to the Loeb-measure forms of Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.5; ns-WWKL0 proves countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure, Riemann integrability of bounded continuous functions and a monotone convergence form of Ascoli's lemma (Lemma 4.7). Also: ns-BASIC is conservative over RCA0 (Theorem 2.4) and ns-WKL0 over WKL0 (Theorem 2.6); LMP is not implied by ns-BASIC plus any true L2 sentence (Remark 3.8).

statement.name: Loeb measure property
statement.definition: If a nonstandard binary tree T* has positive Loeb measure at some nonstandard length omega, then there is a standard function f: N -> 2 with f[n] in T* for all standard n.
statement.facts: Nonstandard counterpart of WWKL; over ns-BASIC it is equivalent to the statements of Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.5 (standard part of positive Loeb measure sets, Loeb measure of st^{-1} of open sets, integral as standard part of nonstandard Riemann sums).

statement.name: Existence of a set of Archimedean representatives for an ordered abelian group
statement.definition: For an ordered abelian group G, Archimedean equivalence a ≈ b means there are n, m with |na| ≥ |b| and |mb| ≥ |a|. A set X ⊂ G is a set of Archimedean representatives if every g in G is Archimedean equivalent to some x in X and distinct elements of X are not Archimedean equivalent. The statement: every ordered abelian group has such a set.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3: over RCA0, for any ordered abelian group G (the proof uses a computable such G), ACA0 is equivalent to the existence of a set of Archimedean representatives for G. Lemma 3.2: over RCA0 this is equivalent to the existence of the set {<g,h> | g ≈ h}. Corollary 3.4: there is a computable ordered abelian group for which every set of Archimedean representatives computes 0'.

statement.name: Hahn's embedding theorem for ordered abelian groups
statement.loc: Section 4, Hahn's Theorem (formal version) before Theorem 4.4
statement.definition: For every ordered abelian group G there are a linear order T and a sequence of Archimedean ordered subgroups K_t (t in T) of G such that G is order isomorphic to a Hahn subgroup (a subgroup of the unrestricted sum of the K_t with the cut property, all supports well ordered, ordered reverse lexicographically) of the sum over T of K_t.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.4: over RCA0, Hahn's Theorem is equivalent to ACA0. Proposition 4.5 proves the reversal (Hahn's Theorem implies ACA0 over RCA0); Section 5 proves Hahn's Theorem in ACA0.

statement.notation: Every torsion free abelian group is orderable
statement.name: Orderability of torsion free abelian groups
statement.definition: Every torsion free abelian group admits a linear order compatible with the group operation (an ordered abelian group structure).
statement.facts: Theorem 1.2 (Hatzikiriakou, Simpson, cited): over RCA0 this is equivalent to WKL0. Theorem 1.1 (Downey, Kurtz): there is a computable torsion free abelian group with no computable order.

statement.name: Holder's theorem for Archimedean ordered groups
statement.definition: Every Archimedean ordered group is isomorphic to an ordered subgroup of (R, +) indexed by the group, for which +A and <=A are the group operation and order.
statement.facts: Stated as provable in RCA0 (citing Solomon [9] for the proof).

statement.name: Complement of a divisible subgroup of an abelian group
statement.definition: If D is a divisible subgroup of an abelian group G, then G = D + A for some subgroup A.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.14 (cited from Simpson, Lemma VI.4.2): provable in ACA0.

statement.name: Stable ascending/descending chain principle (type ω+ω*)
statement.definition: Every stable linear order L (with domain a subset of ω) with infinitely many small and infinitely many large elements has an infinite ascending or descending chain.
statement.facts: SADC ≤sW SADS and SADC ≤sW General-ADC; computable instances of SADC have low solutions (per the proof of Theorem 17(3)); General-ADC ≰W SADS (Theorem 17(2)). The catalogue entry sadc ("every infinite stable linear order has ...") may correspond to the paper's General-ADC rather than to this SADC.

statement.name: ADS for stable linear orders (any stable order)
statement.definition: Every stable linear order L (every element small or large; type ω+k, k+ω* or ω+ω*) has an infinite ascending or descending sequence.
statement.facts: SADS ≤sW General-ADS ≤sW ADS; ADC ≰W General-ADS (Theorem 17(3)); equivalent to ADS, SADS, SADC, General-ADC under ≤c.

statement.name: ADC for stable linear orders (any stable order)
statement.definition: Every stable linear order L has an infinite ascending or descending chain.
statement.facts: SADC ≤sW General-ADC ≤sW ADC and General-ADC ≤sW General-ADS; General-ADC ≰W SADS (Theorem 17(2)). Possibly the catalogue sadc.

statement.notation: Every set is contained in a countable coded ω-model of ACA
statement.name: Existence of countable coded ω-models of ACA containing a given set
statement.definition: For every set X there is a countable coded ω-model M = (N,S,∈,+,·,0,1,<) with S = {(W)_n : n in N} of arithmetic comprehension (ACA) such that X in S (Definition 3.3).
statement.facts: Lemma 3.4: over RCA0 it is equivalent to the ω-jump axiom of ACA0+ (every set X has an ω-jump Y with (Y)_0 = X and (Y)_{n+1} = TJ((Y)_n)). Theorem 4.1: RCA0 + ∀X[WO(X) → WO(εX)] proves it.

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for trees defined by bounded formulae
statement.definition: Scheme Tree∞(A_x) → ∃X (Path(X) ∧ ∀x (x ∈ X → A(x))) for A a bounded (Σb∞) formula, over binary words 2^{<ω}; every infinite tree of 0-1 words defined by a bounded formula has an infinite path.
statement.facts: Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA + Σb∞-WKL is Π02-conservative over Σb1-NIA (Theorem 2). Σb1-NIA + Σb∞-WKL proves BΣb∞ (Proposition 5); the first-order part of Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA + Σb∞-WKL is Σb1-NIA + BΣb∞ (Theorem 7); the theory is Π11-conservative over Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA + BΣb∞ (Corollary 9); BTFA + Σb∞-WKL is Π11-conservative over BTFA (Theorem 10 ii). This is a bounded-arithmetic setting (binary words, polynomial-time functions), not WKL over RCA0.

statement.name: Collection scheme for bounded formulae
statement.definition: ∀x ≤ a ∃y A(x,y) → ∃z ∀x ≤ a ∃y ≤ z A(x,y), A a bounded formula (equivalent over Σb1-NIA to the variant (S2) with x ≡ a).
statement.facts: Σb1-NIA + BΣb∞ is conservative over Σb1-NIA for Π02-sentences (Corollary 6); it is exactly the first-order strength of Σb∞-WKL (Theorem 7).

statement.name: Base Theory for Feasible Analysis
statement.definition: Σb1-NIA + BΣb∞ + the comprehension scheme ($): ∀x (∃y A(x,y) ↔ ∀z ¬B(x,z)) → ∃X ∀x (x ∈ X ↔ ∃y A(x,y)), A, B Σb1.
statement.facts: BTFA is Π02-conservative over Σb1-NIA (Theorem 10 i); BTFA + Σb∞-WKL is Π11-conservative over BTFA (Theorem 10 ii); (2^{<ω}, Δ01) is its smallest model with standard first-order part.

statement.name: NP ∩ co-NP comprehension
statement.definition: ∀x (A(x) ↔ ¬B(x)) → ∃X ∀x (x ∈ X ↔ A(x)) for Σb1 formulae A, B with parameters.
statement.facts: Σb1-NIA + ∇b1-CA is first-order conservative over Σb1-NIA (Lemma 1).

statement.name: Notation induction axiom for Σb1 formulae (binary tree theory, equivalent to Buss' S^1_2)
statement.definition: Basic axioms on the language (ε, 0, 1, concatenation, x×y, initial subword) plus induction on notation A(ε) ∧ ∀x (A(x) → A(x0) ∧ A(x1)) → ∀x A(x) for Σb1 formulae A.
statement.facts: Provably total Σb1-definable functions are the polynomial-time computable functions; base theory of the paper.

statement.name: Universal transfer principle of ERNA
statement.definition: For quantifier-free phi(x) in the standard language of ERNA: (forall^st x) phi(x) -> (forall x) phi(x).
statement.facts: Equivalent in ERNA to bar transfer (Theorem 8), to the continuity and equicontinuity principles (Theorems 18, 19), and to the sequential nonstandard versions of IVT, MVT, IMV, the Weierstrass extremum theorem and the Peano existence theorem (Theorems 23, 26, 28, 39, 40, 46, 50, 53); these are results in ERNA (a nonstandard system over I Delta0 + exp), not over RCA0.

statement.name: Sequential mean value theorem
statement.definition: For a sequence of functions phi_n continuous on [0,1], differentiable on (0,1) with phi_n(0)=phi_n(1)=0, there is a sequence x_n in [0,1] with phi_n'(x_n) = 0 for all n.
statement.facts: Stated to be equivalent to WKL0 (due to T. Yamazaki, unpublished); the paper also notes MVT is provable in RCA0 by Hardin and Velleman [11, Theorem 4].

statement.notation: every countable poset has a maximal filter
statement.name: Existence of maximal filters on countable posets
statement.definition: Every countable poset has a filter (upward closed, any two elements have a common lower bound in the filter) that is not contained in a strictly larger filter.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Corollaries 2.2 and 2.4, from Theorems 2.1 and 2.3). Computable version: every computable poset has a Delta^0_2 maximal filter (Thm 2.1), there is a computable poset with no Sigma^0_1 or Pi^0_1 maximal filter (Thm 2.5), and one on which every maximal filter computes 0' (Thm 2.3, 0' <=wtt F).

statement.notation: every countable poset has an unbounded filter
statement.name: Existence of unbounded filters on countable posets
statement.definition: Every countable poset has a filter F such that no p outside F is a lower bound of all elements of F.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Corollary 3.3, from Theorem 3.2). Computable version: every computable poset has a Sigma^0_1 unbounded filter (Thm 3.1), there is one with no Pi^0_1 unbounded filter (Thm 3.4), and one on which every unbounded filter computes 0' (Thm 3.2). RCA0 proves every countable poset has an unbounded enumerated filter.

statement.notation: extension of sequences of enumerated filters to unbounded enumerated filters
statement.name: Uniform extension of enumerated filters to unbounded enumerated filters
statement.definition: If <P_i> is a sequence of countable posets and each F_i is an enumerated filter on P_i (a function from N to P whose range is a filter), then there is a sequence <G_i> with G_i an unbounded enumerated filter on P_i extending F_i.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.6). The single-poset version (every enumerated filter on a countable poset extends to an unbounded enumerated filter) is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 3.5).

statement.notation: every subset of a countable poset has an upward closure
statement.name: Existence of upward closures in countable posets
statement.definition: For every subset F of a countable poset P, the set {q in P : exists p in F, p <= q} exists. Also considered for linearly ordered subsets F only.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0, and also to the version restricted to linearly ordered subsets (Corollary 4.2, from Theorem 4.1: a computable poset with a computable linearly ordered subset whose upward closure one-one computes 0').
